author: antonleykin
title: OptionalComponentsPresent set to false because of the dependency?
note: stands -- there is no propagation -- but the stated mechanism is not what happens, and anton's own title carries a question mark. Tested with two throwaway packages on 1.26.06-40-gd8e86d689d: with OptTwo declaring OptionalComponentsPresent => false, OptOne comes out true under PackageImports and true under PackageExports alike, so nothing propagates in either direction, and check "OptOne" runs while check "OptTwo" skips. What actually forces false is m2/packages.m2:360, 'if opts.OptionalComponentsPresent === null then opts = opts ++ {OptionalComponentsPresent => opts.CacheExampleOutput =!= true}': a package that sets CacheExampleOutput => true silently gets OptionalComponentsPresent => false and its tests silently skipped. NumericalSchubertCalculus.m2:36 sets exactly that. His workaround is still in the tree and has decayed: lines 1-4 of NumericalSchubertCalculus.m2 are a verbatim copy of lines 1-4 of PHCpack.m2, added in b436e6ddfe on 2021-01-22, the day he filed this -- and the two copies have drifted, PHCpack requiring phc >= 2.4.77 since ad6ea46aee (2020-06-26) while the copy still requires >= 2.3.80. So the ask, that a package inherit its dependency's optional-component status, is unimplemented, and the duplication it forces has already produced an inconsistency.

author: DanGrayson
title: a new problem: notice the "bad prompt":
note: reproduces verbatim on 1.26.06-40-gd8e86d689d, via Doug's 2024 minimal case rather than Dan's matroid script. Feeding 'alarm 1;' and then waiting three seconds before the next line gives exactly the transcript in the body: 'i2 : ' then '<--bad prompt--> : 55'. It needs a genuine idle prompt -- with stdin from a file M2 reads the next line at once and the alarm surfaces as 'error: alarm occurred' instead, so a plain redirect will not show it. Diagnosis in the thread is complete and unacted on: pzinn worked out and Dan confirmed that ZZ#{Standard, InputPrompt} must return a string or a small integer, and the fallback prints <--bad prompt--> when it returns anything else; SIGALRM arriving while the prompt is being computed puts it in that state. Related #1392 (alarm sometimes not caught), open. Label Interpreter is already right.
